text: Tonight, before bed, name the one moment today when fear made the choice for you. What did it cost?
Looking back on today, which decision did you carry around unmade, and what did carrying it cost you?
Which hour of today did you spend as though your time were unlimited?
What did you avoid saying plainly today, and who deserved to hear it?
Before sleep tonight, which small promise to yourself did you quietly drop?

excerpt: Answer the hardest message before the easy ones
text: Reading "Answer the hardest message before the easy ones" again, which hour of today would you take back?
When I open my laptop tomorrow morning, I will spend the first twenty minutes on the thing I keep deferring.
When the first irritating message lands in my inbox today, I will name the feeling before I reply to it.
When I catch myself opening a tab out of boredom, I will shut the laptop and walk to the window.
When someone thanks me today, I will name the specific thing I am grateful to them for.
When I feel the pull to over-explain in the meeting, I will say the shorter true sentence instead.
Picture the outcome you dread arriving exactly as you imagine it, then say plainly what you would do the following morning.
Assume the delay lasts forever. Say in one sentence what you would build in the meantime.
Take the criticism as half accurate and write down the half worth keeping.
Treat today as a rehearsal rather than the performance, and name what you would practise differently.
Suppose the loudest worry is right about the facts and wrong about the consequences. What changes?
Who in your life most needs to hear this today, and why would it land for them?
Which idea you saved earlier this year says the same thing in other words?
Where else in your week does this same pattern show up, and what is it costing you there?
